title: A Distant Star is Slowly Snacking on a Brown Dwarf - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyA Distant Star is Slowly Snacking on a Brown DwarfThis absorption could take billions of yearsDNBy David Nield11:00 AM CDT on October 8, 2026Add Nautilus to GooglePlanets and stars usually have one of two kinds of relationship: Either a planet orbits its star in a fixed and stable circuit, or it flies too close to the sun (literally) and gets consumed by stellar wind and fire.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayBut now, for the first time, astronomers have directly observed an in-between state, a red dwarf star that’s absorbing material from a nearby brown dwarf, but very, very slowly. The transfer of material (or “accretion”) is happening at such a leisurely rate, it might be billions of years before the brown dwarf disappears altogether.Read more: “This Spectacular Star Field Hides Brown Dwarfs That Never Ignite”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
